**Status:** Upgrade Phase 6 (canonical sample and rewritten landing page) implemented on the verified Phase 5 baseline.
**Owner:** Engineering.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 against the Phase 6 verification matrix recorded in `docs/EVIDENCE.md`.

## 1. System shape

```text
Browser
  ├─ /            landing page (eager)
  ├─ /demo        guided sample (lazy chunk)
  └─ /workshop    real workshop (lazy chunk)
        │
        │ same-origin fetch /api/*
        │ Basic Auth in hosted modes; x-ub-session-token on protected API routes
        ▼
Hono server (src/server/app.ts)
  ├─ /api/health                 public, minimal
  ├─ /api/mode                   public mode descriptor
  ├─ /api/session                token issue (loopback/local, Basic Auth/private)
  ├─ /api/runtime                effective limits/retention
  ├─ /api/engine                 connection/engine summary
  ├─ /api/connection*            check, configure (local only), reset
  ├─ /api/opencode/*             discovery, project-owned sessions, permissions, usage
  ├─ /api/engine/selection       persist a discovered model allowed by project policy
  ├─ /api/model-preferences      access mode, privacy preference, optional spending limit
  ├─ /api/project, /api/export   snapshot/approved plan; workspace paths omitted
  ├─ /api/project/source*        select source; explicitly confirm managed remote import
  ├─ /api/events                 authenticated bounded SSE snapshots
  ├─ /api/messages, /api/approvals, /api/sections/*
  ├─ /api/memory                 add or correct project memory; corrections supersede
  ├─ /api/runs*                  queue, inspect, cancel, reconcile
  └─ static dist/web             contained SPA fallback for HTML navigation
        │
        ▼
OpenCode 2.x server over loopback (or an explicit allowlisted remote)
  ├─ model/provider/agent discovery
  ├─ native tools, permissions, sessions, interruption
  └─ isolated demo workspace
```

Unfinished Business never implements a second agent loop, inference client, general command executor, or transcript store. OpenCode owns those. The app owns workflow state, approvals, dependency invalidation, evidence references, security policy, and the interface.

## 2. Frontend routing and bundles

`src/web/routes.ts` is the pure route resolver:

| Path | Route | Rendering |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `landing` | Eager `LandingPage` |
| `/demo` | `demo` | Lazy `DemoPage` |
| `/workshop` | `workshop` | Lazy `WorkshopPage` |
| anything else | `landing` | Landing fallback |

`src/web/App.tsx` reads `window.location.pathname`, listens for `popstate`, updates `document.title` and `document.documentElement.dataset.route`, and scrolls to the top on route change. Navigations are ordinary anchors, so they work without a client router.

Measured production chunks after Phase 5 (2026-11-01):

- initial `index-*.js`: 195.5 KiB gzip;
- `WorkshopPage-*.js`: 69.1 KiB gzip (includes source onboarding, discovery, revision review, safe Markdown, project memory, and diffs);
- `DemoPage-*.js`: 12.5 KiB gzip;
- `SpiritStageTabs-*.js`: 3.6 KiB gzip;
- CSS: 17.0 KiB gzip (18 KiB budget; all JS budget remains 290 KiB).

The workshop presents one primary task at a time. A compact header carries the connection and selected model. The project outline is a collapsible drawer. Activity & results appears only when an operation or check exists, opens automatically for an active or abandoned run, and is organized into Progress, Changes, and Checks. Native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, and provider payloads live under Technical details. Project memory is a separate editable drawer; raw transcripts stay inside Advanced diagnostics. The previous permanent right rail and Session notes panel are gone.

Provider failures render as a dedicated card with what happened, saved-work state, repair action, retry/change-model controls, and technical disclosure. Activity & results retains a compact provider-error line even after the card is dismissed. The visual layer changes did not alter stage and approval semantics.

## 3. Static serving and assets

`src/server/index.ts` serves `dist/web` when it exists:

- `/` and HTML navigations → `index.html`;
- real files → their content type, with long-lived caching;
- unknown non-HTML paths → 404, not a 200 HTML fallback;
- `/api/*` is never served from disk;
- paths are resolved through `realpath` and must stay under `dist/web`;
- private state under `UB_DATA_DIR` is never in the static root.

Public hero assets are produced by `scripts/build-hero-assets.py` into `public/assets/hero/`; Vite copies them into `dist/web/assets/hero/`. The `<picture>` element selects portrait/wide crops and carries explicit dimensions.

|---|---|
| `src/server/app.ts` | HTTP pipeline, route validation, mode enforcement, SSE, error mapping |

| `src/server/opencode/connection.ts` | Connection settings, discovery, model access policy and resolution |

name: Verify application

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify (${{ matrix.platform }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            platform: linux-x64
          - os: macos-15
            platform: darwin-arm64
          - os: macos-15-intel
            platform: darwin-x64

    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.14.0
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Resolve the platform OpenCode CLI
        run: npm run diagnose:platform

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

name: Verify application

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify (${{ matrix.platform }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            platform: linux-x64
          - os: macos-15
            platform: darwin-arm64
          - os: macos-15-intel
            platform: darwin-x64

    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.14.0
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Resolve the platform OpenCode CLI
        run: npm run diagnose:platform

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Test workspace path safety and platform resolution
        run: npm run test:platform

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Smoke-test the OpenCode server
        run: npm run smoke:opencode

      - name: Preserve the deployable browser artifact
        if: matrix.platform == 'linux-x64'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: unfinished-business-web-${{ github.sha }}
          path: dist/web
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

# Unfinished Business

**Turn unfinished ideas into hackathon-ready builds.**

Unfinished Business is an OpenCode-powered hackathon project builder. Four friendly spirits guide one idea through a clear proposal, an approved plan, a real bounded build, and evidence you can defend.

![Ghostlight Hacker Workshop landing page](tests/visual/snapshots/landing-wide.png)

## What it is

- A **landing page** at `/` built around the hero, the four-stage workflow, one sample project, why OpenCode does the coding, local setup and privacy, and a short FAQ.
- A **guided sample** at `/demo`: one versioned Driftwatch fixture — an abandoned open-source CLI revived through clarification, a plan, one bounded change, a recorded check, and Witness findings. It has Play/Pause, step, replay, reset, four inspectable spirit tabs, and an optional 90-second presentation mode at `/demo?presentation=1`. It does not call a model or read a repository.
- The **real workshop** at `/workshop`, which connects to a local OpenCode server and records what actually happened.
- A **first-run connection and discovery flow** that checks a supported OpenCode server, lists the models/providers/agents it actually reports, and lets the builder choose a model and reported reasoning variant. Provider API keys stay inside OpenCode.
- A **read-only hosted sample** and a **private hosted** mode. Neither reaches into a visitor's local repository.
- A versioned **schema v7** contract for explicit project sources, field-level Oracle intake answers, structured facts/decisions/assumptions with editable superseding corrections, structured proposals, reviewable candidate section revisions, model preferences, provider errors, and recoverable operations. Explicit v1–v6 migrations keep older projects usable.
- **Reviewable Architect revisions**: every section has a content contract; a change request generates a candidate with a summary and complete Markdown draft. The user inspects a unified or side-by-side diff, then accepts, requests another revision, or discards. Only an accepted candidate replaces the current draft, and approval remains a separate exact-version action.
- **Focused workshop**: one primary task at a time, a collapsible project outline, a contextual Activity & results drawer, an editable Project memory drawer, and a compact model/connection header. Empty technical panels no longer occupy permanent space.
- **Activity & results**: the former Run Inspector is organized into Progress, Changes, and Checks. Native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, provider payloads, and the transcript stay under Technical details or Advanced diagnostics.
- **Editable project memory**: decisions, user answers, assumptions, constraints, and unresolved questions are visible in one place. A correction supersedes the prior entry without changing an approval, section draft, Maker scope, or native run.
- **Focused, multi-turn Oracle discovery**: every fresh project chooses new work, a validated local repository, a credential-free remote repository import, or saved work before discovery. Oracle asks at most three explained questions per turn and proposes only after essential intake is known or the user explicitly accepts stated assumptions.
- **Observable, cancellable, recoverable runs**: every Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness run is a persisted asynchronous operation with live progress phases, elapsed time, and Continue waiting / Reconcile / Open in OpenCode / Cancel / Retry / Mark abandoned controls in Activity & results. A timed-out or restarted run never permanently blocks the project; reconciliation retrieves and validates the actual late response or diff and applies it exactly once.

OpenCode supplies the agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, execution, interruption, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, evidence views, the onboarding/discovery flow, and the Ghostlight interface. It does **not** ship a second coding harness or a general command executor.

| Spirit | Role |
|---|---|
| Oracle | Choose the project source, collect structured answers over focused turns, and prepare a fact/decision/assumption-aware proposal |
| Architect | Draft one planning section and wait for approval of that exact version |
| Maker | Perform an approved, bounded native edit through OpenCode |
| Witness | Inspect evidence in a fresh session and prepare honest review drafts |

## Runtime modes

**Hosted sample** — `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo`. A public, read-only sample. It has no OpenCode process, provider credentials, session token, visitor persistence, or repository access. Every non-GET `/api/*` request returns `403 DEMO_READ_ONLY`.

**Private hosted** — `REDACTED`. A password-protected Render or self-hosted instance with a private disk and a loopback OpenCode child. Maker edits the server's isolated demo workspace. A hosted browser cannot edit a visitor's machine.

**Local workshop** — `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=local` (default). The browser app, local API, and pinned OpenCode server run on the builder's machine over loopback. Oracle source onboarding validates local directories and can import a public HTTPS repository into an app-managed workspace after explicit confirmation. Maker's edit remains bounded to the isolated demo workspace; selecting a source does not authorize implementation in that repository.

The landing page has one primary action, **Try the example** (`/demo`), and one secondary action, **Run locally** (`/workshop`). A quiet setup link goes to the tested local commands. The sample is always labeled as recorded; the live native session remains `NOT_RUN`. The 90-second playback stays available inside `/demo` but is no longer a competing landing CTA.

Models are discovered from OpenCode rather than assumed. New projects default to **All accessible models**, so any model OpenCode reports as available can be selected. A project can deliberately switch to **Free and local only**, which blocks paid and unknown-price remote models. Paid or unknown-price remote models require an explicit first-use confirmation; the app never silently substitutes a model or makes a paid request without that confirmation. An optional USD session spending limit can be set, and the deployment can impose a stricter `UB_MAX_SESSION_COST_USD` ceiling. Cost is checked against the value OpenCode reports; an unknown-price provider may report it only after a request.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Linux, Node **22.14+**, npm, and a supported OpenCode 2.x server. Copying `.env.example` to `.env` is optional for local work; the first-run wizard can hold the server password in memory.

```bash
npm ci
cp .env.example .env   # optional
```

Terminal 1 — OpenCode:

```bash
./node_modules/@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline/bin/opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

Terminal 2 — API:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Terminal 3 — interface:

```bash
npm run dev:web
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`. The first-run wizard asks for the server URL and the password printed by `opencode serve`; provider accounts are connected inside OpenCode with `/connect`, and the model list comes from OpenCode's catalog.

For a single production process:

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:4200/`. The detailed, tested guide is [docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md](docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md). All state and mutation API routes require the browser session token; the browser client obtains it from `/api/session` automatically.

## Verification

Run the release matrix:

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run budget
npm run test:visual
```

Current results (2026-11-01, Node 22.22.1, no live provider inference):

- **186 unit/integration/component tests pass**.
- **20 Playwright visual/accessibility tests pass** with committed snapshots, including the rewritten landing wide/narrow captures, the guided sample wide/narrow/presentation captures, the canonical sample-consistency check, and the reorganized Activity & results view.
- Initial JS is **201.3 KiB gzip**; all JS **279.9 KiB**; CSS **17.0 KiB gzip**; all hero variants **581.2 KiB** total. The all-JS budget remains 290 KiB and CSS remains within its 18 KiB budget.
- Keyboard focus order, dialog Escape, setup tab arrow keys, drawer operation, 200% text zoom, 390px overflow, reduced motion, and token contrast are checked.
- Sample playback, reset isolation, fixture/schema drift, 90-second timing, tab inspection, no-network behavior, canonical landing/demo consistency, and hosted-sample mutation rejection are covered.
- State migration deterministically upgrades schema v1, both supported v2 shapes, schema v3, schema v4, schema v5, and schema v6 to v7 without dropping proposals, approvals, transcripts, operations, evidence, selected model data, provider policy, limits, or candidate history.
- Project-source paths, incomplete intake, explained question limits, explicit assumptions, proposal provenance, reload persistence, correction history, and project-memory corrections are covered.
- Section contracts, candidate creation/supersede, accept/reject, stale approvals, base-version conflicts, safe Markdown rendering, and unified/side-by-side diffs are covered.
- Model access policy, paid/unknown-price confirmation, optional spending limits, provider failure classification/redaction, and runtime confirmation gates are covered.
- Local and hosted-sample smoke journeys pass; the hosted sample makes no inference call and rejects mutation.
- OpenCode 2.0.32 live compatibility probe passed (version, catalog, and disposable session create/read/remove; no prompt or model call).
- Production dependency audit at `--audit-level=high` passes. `npm audit` still reports six moderate `glob`/`minimatch` advisories reachable through the Sentry bundler plugin during developer builds; the suggested fix is a breaking Sentry downgrade and was not applied.

`npm run test:visual` needs a Chromium executable. It prefers `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE`, then system Chrome/Chromium, then Playwright's browser.

## Status and limitations

The prior release phases remain integrated. Upgrade Phase 6 rewrites the public story around one canonical Driftwatch sample: the landing page now has one primary action, a four-stage workflow, a coherent abandoned-open-source sample, a direct OpenCode explanation, local setup and privacy, and a short FAQ. The non-interactive idea-to-tool recommendation block was removed, and the technical sample disclosure moved under details. Upgrade Phase 5 remains the focused workshop: one main task, a collapsible outline, contextual Activity & results, editable Project memory, a compact model/connection header, and lazy Advanced diagnostics. Schema v7 is unchanged.

Known limitations:

- The application is a trusted single-project tool, not a multi-tenant sandbox. Remote imports are public HTTPS clones into a managed local directory; private/authenticated repositories, shared-host isolation, arbitrary Maker access to selected repositories, and remote browser-to-local pairing remain deferred.
- Maker edits only `UB_DATA_DIR/demo-workspace`; the Node check is not an OS sandbox.
- Generated section review supports a deliberately small, safe Markdown subset (headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, links, tables, and code), not full CommonMark or raw HTML. Contract validation checks structure and topic coverage, not prose quality.
- Model availability, pricing, quota, training terms, and billing are controlled by OpenCode/provider. The spending limit only checks cost OpenCode reports after a session; unknown-price providers may bill before that value is visible.
- The workspace privacy preference records intent; the app cannot attest every provider's training/retention contract. Provider rejections that mention training/data policy are explained as `PROVIDER_DATA_POLICY`.
- Advanced diagnostics load only when opened. Permission polling is best-effort; a pending request remains visible in Activity & results and the contextual permission alert, but a provider-side change can lag by one refresh interval.
- Backboard is not integrated and no partner category is claimed for installation alone. Sentry is configured but live release/source-map/trace verification requires authorized credentials and a deployment.
- No public hosted URL, recorded video, published article, or submission is asserted by this repository.
- A real recorded demonstration and final submission packaging remain separate acceptance work.

- [Product brief](docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md) — positioning, landing claims, three usage paths.
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — routes, trust boundaries, persistence, modes, security.

- [Tool catalog](docs/TOOL_CATALOG.md) — selected tools and honest availability.

- [Demo and submission](docs/DEMO_AND_SUBMISSION.md) — scenario, fixture provenance, playback/reset, exact claims, video beats, disclosure.
- [Decisions](docs/DECISIONS.md) — product, interface, demo, and hardening decisions.
- [Changelog](docs/CHANGELOG.md) — released changes.
- [Evidence index](docs/EVIDENCE.md) — requirements-to-evidence matrix, commands, limitations.

History and provenance:

- [Engineering blueprint](docs/history/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md) — superseded planning record.
- [Product idea packet](docs/history/Unfinished-Business-Idea-Packet-v1.md) — approved discovery record.

- [Complete local prompt set](docs/prompts/README.md) — runtime Prompts 0–3 and project overrides.

## Development policy

- Repository: [kernelKain/unfinished-business](https://github.com/kernelKain/unfinished-business).
- Work on the existing `main` branch. Do not create phase branches.
- Complete and verify each phase, then make one commit for that phase before starting the next phase.
- Steps are work/checklist units, not individual commits. Commit subjects describe the change without phase or step numbering.
- Preserve unrelated changes. A blocked commit blocks entry to the next implementation phase; do not bypass access restrictions.
- No fabricated testimonials, usage figures, awards, or live-run claims.
- No second coding harness, authenticated repository connector, arbitrary Maker repository mount, or public arbitrary-execution sandbox.

## Delivery

The first release targets a local browser on Linux. A real recorded demonstration and a reproducible local-start guide provide judge access; hosted code execution is outside this release. Backboard, Sentry Agent Tracing, and Entire remain selected partner targets, with qualification conditional on meaningful actual use and evidence. Publication, deployment, domain registration, credit claiming, and submission remain pending separate authorization.

# Hosted and private deployment

**Status:** Deployment procedure reviewable; no deployment or public URL authorized or asserted.
**Owner:** Engineering/deployment.
**Last verified:** 2026-10-31 by static Blueprint/config review and a local hosted-demo smoke run.

## Two hosted shapes

| Shape | Mode | Public? | OpenCode | Persistence | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted sample | `hosted-demo` | Yes, read-only | None | No visitor state | `render.demo.yaml` |
| Private workshop | `private-hosted` | Password-protected | Loopback child | Private persistent disk | `render.yaml` |

Both serve the same build:

- `/` — landing page;
- `/demo` — labeled recorded Driftwatch sample;
- `/workshop` — real workshop (read-only notice in demo mode);
- `/api/*` — validated API.

A hosted instance is **not** a public sandbox, a remote mount of a visitor's checkout, proof of free-model availability, or a substitute for the local real-execution demonstration.

## Hosted sample behavior

`UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo` serves the public guided example without OpenCode, provider credentials, a repository, a session token, or visitor persistence:

| Behavior | Hosted sample |
|---|---|
| Routes | `/`, `/demo`, `/workshop` public; `/api/health` and `/api/mode` public |
| API reads | `/api/project` and `/api/export` return the versioned fixture |
| API writes | Every non-GET `/api/*` request returns `403 DEMO_READ_ONLY` before a body is parsed |
| Session token | `/api/session` returns `403`; no token is issued |
| OpenCode | `/api/opencode/*` is unavailable; no connection object is constructed |
| Connection | `/api/connection` returns a read-only demo status with no engine address |
| Repository | None. Sample workspace is `demo://driftwatch` |
| Persistence | No visitor state is written; reload returns the same sample |
| Inference | Zero model/provider calls |
| Reset | Changes only client playback state |

Do not set `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` or start `render-start.ts` for the demo. Use `npm start` with `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo`; `render.demo.yaml` does that on a free service. The server rejection is independent of the UI.

### Local review of the demo

```bash
npm run build
UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo \
UB_HOST=127.0.0.1 \
UB_PORT=4319 \
UB_DATA_DIR=/tmp/opencode/ub-demo-smoke \
node --import tsx src/server/start.ts
```

Then verify:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/health
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/project
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/session          # 403
curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"actionId":"demo","expectedRevision":0}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/runs                                                   # 403 DEMO_READ_ONLY
```

The Phase 9 smoke run passed these checks and confirmed `/demo` returns HTML.

## Private hosted configuration

`render.yaml` defines one paid Linux x64 Node web service:

| Setting | Value/behavior |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Node 22.14 |
| Plan | `0.5c-512mb`; persistent disk required |
| Build | `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` |
| Start | `npm run start:render` |
| Health check | `/api/health` (public, minimal) |
| Disk | 1 GB at `/var/data` |
| Host binding | `UB_HOST=0.0.0.0` |
| Deployment mode | `REDACTED` |
| Data | `UB_DATA_DIR=/var/data/unfinished-business` |

npm start

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run budget
npm run test:visual

- Complete and verify each phase, then make one commit for that phase before starting the next phase.

**Owner:** Engineering/deployment.
**Last verified:** 2026-10-31 by static Blueprint/config review and a local hosted-demo smoke run.

## Two hosted shapes

| Shape | Mode | Public? | OpenCode | Persistence | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted sample | `hosted-demo` | Yes, read-only | None | No visitor state | `render.demo.yaml` |
| Private workshop | `private-hosted` | Password-protected | Loopback child | Private persistent disk | `render.yaml` |

Both serve the same build:

- `/` — landing page;
- `/demo` — labeled recorded Driftwatch sample;
- `/workshop` — real workshop (read-only notice in demo mode);
- `/api/*` — validated API.

A hosted instance is **not** a public sandbox, a remote mount of a visitor's checkout, proof of free-model availability, or a substitute for the local real-execution demonstration.

## Hosted sample behavior

`UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo` serves the public guided example without OpenCode, provider credentials, a repository, a session token, or visitor persistence:

| Behavior | Hosted sample |
|---|---|
| Routes | `/`, `/demo`, `/workshop` public; `/api/health` and `/api/mode` public |
| API reads | `/api/project` and `/api/export` return the versioned fixture |
| API writes | Every non-GET `/api/*` request returns `403 DEMO_READ_ONLY` before a body is parsed |
| Session token | `/api/session` returns `403`; no token is issued |
| OpenCode | `/api/opencode/*` is unavailable; no connection object is constructed |
| Connection | `/api/connection` returns a read-only demo status with no engine address |
| Repository | None. Sample workspace is `demo://driftwatch` |
| Persistence | No visitor state is written; reload returns the same sample |
| Inference | Zero model/provider calls |
| Reset | Changes only client playback state |

Do not set `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` or start `render-start.ts` for the demo. Use `npm start` with `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo`; `render.demo.yaml` does that on a free service. The server rejection is independent of the UI.

```bash
npm run build
UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo \
UB_HOST=127.0.0.1 \
UB_PORT=4319 \
UB_DATA_DIR=/tmp/opencode/ub-demo-smoke \
node --import tsx src/server/start.ts
```

Then verify:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/health
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/project
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/session          # 403
curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"actionId":"demo","expectedRevision":0}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:4319/api/runs                                                   # 403 DEMO_READ_ONLY
```

The Phase 9 smoke run passed these checks and confirmed `/demo` returns HTML.

`render.yaml` defines one paid Linux x64 Node web service:

| Setting | Value/behavior |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Node 22.14 |
| Plan | `0.5c-512mb`; persistent disk required |
| Build | `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` |
| Start | `npm run start:render` |
| Health check | `/api/health` (public, minimal) |
| Disk | 1 GB at `/var/data` |
| Host binding | `UB_HOST=0.0.0.0` |
| Deployment mode | `REDACTED` |
| Data | `UB_DATA_DIR=/var/data/unfinished-business` |

## Quick start

Prerequisites: **Linux x64**, **macOS Apple Silicon**, or **macOS Intel**, Node **22.14+**, npm, and a supported OpenCode 2.x server. The pinned `@opencode/cli` package selects the native binary for the host; a compatible global `opencode` on `PATH` is preferred automatically. Copying `.env.example` to `.env` is optional for local work; the first-run wizard can hold the server password in memory.

```bash
npm ci
cp .env.example .env   # optional
```

Terminal 1 — OpenCode (the pinned lockfile binary works on all three supported hosts):

```bash
npx --no-install opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

To use a global install instead:

```bash
# Linux or macOS with npm
npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.0.32

# macOS with Homebrew
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
```

Terminal 2 — API:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Terminal 3 — interface:

```bash
npm run dev:web
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`. The first-run wizard asks for the server URL and the password printed by `opencode serve`; provider accounts are connected inside OpenCode with `/connect`, and the model list comes from OpenCode's catalog.

For a single production process:

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:4200/`. The detailed, tested guide is [docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md](docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md). All state and mutation API routes require the browser session token; the browser client obtains it from `/api/session` automatically.

If OpenCode cannot be resolved, run:

```bash
npm run diagnose:platform   # CLI, platform, version, and permission diagnostics
npm run smoke:opencode      # starts the resolved server, reads /api/info, then stops it
```

# Local setup

**Status:** Linux x64 verified locally; macOS Apple Silicon and macOS Intel verified by the CI matrix.
**Owner:** Engineering.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 on Linux x64 with Node 22.22.1, npm 9.2.0, Git, and the pinned OpenCode 2.0.32 CLI. macOS jobs run the same install, resolution, typecheck, test, build, workspace-safety, and OpenCode smoke steps. This guide is the source for the landing page's setup tabs.

## What you get

- Landing page at `http://127.0.0.1:5173/` (Vite).
- Real workshop at `http://127.0.0.1:5173/workshop`.
- Guided sample at `http://127.0.0.1:5173/demo`.
- API on `http://127.0.0.1:4200`.
- OpenCode on `http://127.0.0.1:4096`.

The browser app does not receive provider credentials or the OpenCode password. The local API connects to OpenCode over loopback.

## Prerequisites

- **Linux x64**, **macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)**, or **macOS Intel (x64)**; Node **22.14+**, npm, and Git (required only for confirmed remote repository imports).
- A supported OpenCode 2.x server. The repository pins the official cross-platform `@opencode/cli@2.0.32` and `@opencode/client@2.0.32`; npm selects the native binary for the host.
- At least one model route that answers on your OpenCode account, or a local model. The free `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` route is still available when the provider reports it, but availability is time-limited and not guaranteed.
- A writable `UB_DATA_DIR` whose demo/spirit child directories stay inside that root. Do not point it at `/`, your home, `/Users`, `/Volumes`, the temporary root, the repository root, or another broad system directory.

Windows, Linux ARM64, and 32-bit hosts are not supported or claimed. `npm run diagnose:platform` reports an unsupported-platform diagnostic before probing any binary.

New projects allow any model OpenCode reports as available. A paid or unknown-price remote model requires an explicit confirmation, and the optional spending limit is enforced only against cost OpenCode reports. There is no silent model substitution or automatic paid fallback.

## 1. Install

```bash
npm ci
```

The lockfile pins React 19, Vite 8, Motion 14, Playwright, the cross-platform OpenCode 2.0.32 CLI, and Sentry. `npm ci` is the reproducible install; use it when verifying a release. The `@opencode/cli` postinstall materializes the native `opencode` binary for Linux x64, macOS arm64, or macOS x64.

## 3. Start OpenCode (terminal 1)

Use the lockfile-installed cross-platform CLI:

```bash
npx --no-install opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

This command is the same on Linux x64, macOS Apple Silicon, and macOS Intel. If you already have a compatible global OpenCode 2.x installation, this is equivalent:

```bash
opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

The application itself prefers a compatible global `opencode` on `PATH`; otherwise it resolves the lockfile-installed binary. If you install globally instead:

```bash
# npm on Linux or macOS
npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.0.32
opencode --version

# Homebrew on macOS
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
opencode --version
```

OpenCode prints a generated server password. Copy it into `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` or enter it in the first-run wizard. Do not commit it.

A full model call was not repeated during the Phase 9 gate. The Phase 9 compatibility probe verified server version, catalog access, and disposable session create/read/remove without inference.

### Platform diagnostics

Run these before opening a support issue:

```bash
npm run diagnose:platform   # executable, source, version, platform support, permission
npm run smoke:opencode      # starts the resolved server, reads /api/info, stops it
```

The diagnostic emits one of:

| Code | Meaning | Repair |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` | Host is not Linux x64, macOS arm64, or macOS x64 | Run on a supported host; do not claim the current host as supported. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_MISSING` | No usable `opencode` on `PATH` and no materialized `@opencode/cli` binary | Run `npm ci`; if install scripts were disabled, reinstall with scripts enabled. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_PERMISSION_DENIED` | A candidate exists but is not executable by this user | Fix ownership/mode or reinstall without `sudo`. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE` | Major version is not 2, or no version was reported | Install `@opencode/cli@2.0.32` or the matching Homebrew tap. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_VERSION_UNTESTED` | A different 2.x patch was found | Use 2.0.32 for the tested surface, or run the live diagnostic. |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_START_FAILED` | The server exited before answering `/api/info` | Check the port, data/config directory permissions, and the CLI version. |

No diagnostic prints the executable path, credentials, prompts, or model output.

# OpenCode integration contract

**Status:** Implemented and locally verified on Linux x64; macOS Apple Silicon and macOS Intel are covered by the CI matrix.
**Owner:** Engineering/integration.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 against Platform Phase 7 and the Phase 5 focused-workshop/OpenCode-controls surface.

This document describes the supported OpenCode surface, not every endpoint OpenCode exposes. OpenCode remains the owner of inference, the agent loop, tools, permissions, and native sessions.

## Supported versions, client, and hosts

| Component | Tested value | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode server | `2.0.32` | Major `2` is accepted. A different `2.x` version is shown as `degraded` with an explicit untested-version warning. Major `1.x`, unparseable versions, and other majors are `incompatible_version`; discovery stops. |
| OpenCode CLI package | `@opencode/cli` `2.0.32` | Official cross-platform package pinned in the lockfile. Its postinstall selects the native binary for the host. |
| `@opencode/client` | `2.0.32` | Exact lockfile version, matched to the pinned server. |
| Node.js | `>=22.14` | Application runtime. |
| Server host | loopback by default | A remote target must use HTTPS, be explicitly allowlisted, and pass DNS/IP policy. |
| Local host platform | Linux x64, macOS arm64, macOS x64 | Declared supported. Linux is verified in this checkout; macOS is gated by the CI jobs below. Windows, Linux ARM64, and 32-bit hosts are not claimed. |

### CLI resolution and Render isolation

`src/server/opencode/executable.ts` is the only runtime resolver. It:

1. honors an explicit `UB_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE`;
2. prefers a compatible global `opencode` found on `PATH` (npm, Homebrew, or a package manager install);
3. falls back to the lockfile-installed `node_modules/@opencode/cli/bin/opencode.exe`;
4. probes `--version` and requires major `2`, warning when the patch is not `2.0.32`;
5. rejects unsupported platforms before probing anything.

The Render/private-hosted supervisor (`src/server/render-start.ts`) uses the same resolver. Its only Render-specific behavior is environment configuration (`OPENCODE_DATA_HOME`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_HOME`, `OPENCODE_PORT`, and the loopback bind). Local development never starts that supervisor and never depends on a Linux executable path. Default XDG locations are derived from `UB_DATA_DIR` or the host temporary directory, not a hardcoded `/tmp` or `/var/data` path.

### Runtime diagnostics

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENCODE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` | error | Host is not Linux x64, macOS arm64, or macOS x64. |
| `OPENCODE_CLI_MISSING` | error | No usable executable on `PATH` or in the local package. |

The Phase 9 smoke run passed these checks and confirmed `/demo` returns HTML.

## Private hosted configuration

`render.yaml` defines one paid Linux x64 Node web service:

| Setting | Value/behavior |
|---|---|
| Runtime | Node 22.14 |
| Plan | `0.5c-512mb`; persistent disk required |
| Build | `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` |
| Start | `npm run start:render` |
| Health check | `/api/health` (public, minimal) |
| Disk | 1 GB at `/var/data` |
| Host binding | `UB_HOST=0.0.0.0` |
| Deployment mode | `REDACTED` |
| Data | `UB_DATA_DIR=/var/data/unfinished-business` |
| Access | `UB_ACCESS_USERNAME` + generated `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` |
| Session token | Generated `UB_SESSION_TOKEN` |
| OpenCode | Generated `OPENCODE_PASSWORD`; loopback `http://127.0.0.1:4096` |
| OpenCode storage | `/var/data/xdg-data`, `/var/data/xdg-config` |
| Origin policy | `RENDER_EXTERNAL_HOSTNAME` supplies the public HTTPS origin |
| Sentry | DSNs and auth token supplied as sync-false secrets |

`npm run start:render` starts the pinned OpenCode baseline binary on loopback, then the Hono server. It forwards termination to both and exits if OpenCode exits unexpectedly. It does not require a build tool on the runtime disk; the binary is pinned in the lockfile.

The private service is **not compatible with Render's free plan** because it needs a persistent disk and enough memory for OpenCode.

## Environment variables

Canonical mode is `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (`local`, `private-hosted`, `hosted-demo`). `UB_MODE` remains a compatibility alias; the legacy `hosted-private` spelling maps to `private-hosted`.

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` | Yes on Render | `private-hosted` for `render.yaml`; `hosted-demo` for `render.demo.yaml`. |
| `UB_HOST` | Yes on Render | `0.0.0.0` behind the proxy. Local mode must stay loopback. |
| `UB_PUBLIC_URL` | Private hosted | Explicit HTTPS origin. Render derives it from `RENDER_EXTERNAL_HOSTNAME`. |
| `UB_ALLOWED_HOSTS` / `UB_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Optional | Additional comma-separated host/origin entries. The public URL host/origin is added automatically. |
| `UB_TRUST_PROXY` | Hosted | Defaults to true in hosted modes; trust `X-Forwarded-*` only behind a controlled proxy. |
| `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD` | Private hosted | Basic Auth password; the server refuses to start without it. |
| `UB_ACCESS_USERNAME` | Recommended | Defaults to `unfinished-business`. |
| `UB_SESSION_TOKEN` | Private hosted | Required; generated by Render. |
| `UB_DATA_DIR` | Yes | Dedicated persistent directory, e.g. `/var/data/unfinished-business`. |
| `UB_MAX_SESSION_COST_USD` | Optional | `unlimited` (default), `disabled`, or `0` for no app ceiling; a positive value sets a deployment-wide USD ceiling. A project limit can be stricter; cost is checked against OpenCode's reported value. |
| `OPENCODE_BASE_URL` | Yes | Keep `http://127.0.0.1:4096` for the private child. Remote targets require HTTPS + allowlist. |
| `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` | Private hosted | Required by `render-start.ts`; passed to OpenCode as both `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`. |
| `OPENCODE_DATA_HOME` / `OPENCODE_CONFIG_HOME` | Private hosted | XDG paths on the persistent disk. |
| `UB_OPENCODE_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | Remote only | Explicit HTTPS host allowlist. |
| `UB_OPENCODE_ALLOWED_PORTS` | Optional | Comma-separated port allowlist. |
| `UB_OPENCODE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK` | Rare | Only when a private network target is intended. |
| `SENTRY_DSN` / `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` | Optional | Public project identifiers, not auth tokens. |
| `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` | Source maps only | Build secret; never `VITE_`-prefixed or committed. |
| `SENTRY_ORG` / `SENTRY_PROJECT` / `SENTRY_URL` | Source maps only | Sentry project/region configuration. |

Do not set `SENTRY_RELEASE` manually on Render; both server and browser derive `unfinished-business@<RENDER_GIT_COMMIT>`.

## Reviewable deployment procedure

No step below was executed in Phase 9. Deployment is a separate authorized action.

1. Push the release commit to the intended repository. Do not push from this worktree without authorization.
2. In Render, create a Blueprint from `render.yaml` (private) or `render.demo.yaml` (public demo).
3. Review the service plan, region, disk mount, health check, and generated secrets before applying.
4. For the private service, supply the Sentry DSNs and optional auth token. Confirm the build fails rather than deploys without source maps when `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is present and required.
5. Apply. Confirm the disk is mounted at `/var/data` and is not the build directory.
6. Wait for `/api/health` to return `{"status":"ok","service":"unfinished-business"}`.
7. For the private service, open the URL and sign in with `unfinished-business` and the generated `UB_ACCESS_PASSWORD`. Confirm HTTPS and the host/origin policy.
8. For the demo, confirm `/api/session` is 403, `/api/project` returns the fixture, a mutation is `403 DEMO_READ_ONLY`, and `/api/engine` reports no OpenCode connection.
9. For the private service, open `/workshop`, run a connection check, and confirm the engine status. Do not claim a model call succeeded until the provider actually returns one.
10. Confirm logs contain correlation IDs but no passwords, prompts, bodies, provider keys, or local paths.
11. Verify Sentry release/source-map association only when authorized credentials and a deployment exist. Check the event release matches the uploaded maps and deploy.
12. Keep the public URL, deployment result, and any partner/competition claim out of documentation until separately verified.

input.newString: `npm run start:render` is the Render/private-hosted process supervisor. It resolves OpenCode through the same cross-platform resolver used locally (preferring a compatible `PATH` install, then the lockfile package), starts it on loopback, then starts the Hono server. Render-specific values live in environment variables (`OPENCODE_DATA_HOME`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_HOME`, `OPENCODE_PORT`, `UB_DATA_DIR`); no Linux-only executable path is embedded in the source. The supervisor forwards termination to both and exits if OpenCode exits unexpectedly. It does not require a build tool on the runtime disk; the binary is pinned in the lockfile.

| U3-04 | Keep the complete Product Discovery prompt and append a persistence adapter | Replace the runtime procedure with a short one-shot JSON prompt | Oracle still needs the full interviewing method; JSON is a storage contract, not the product behavior | Prompt 0 remains first and intact; a detailed adapter requests the richer schema and current structured memory |

| U3-07 | Store field-level answers and assumptions with provenance; supersede corrections | Preserve only the raw transcript; mutate an old memory entry in place | Reloads and corrections need a durable distinction among facts, user decisions, and assumptions | Active memory drives prompts and UI; corrections create a new active entry and mark the prior entry `SUPERSEDED` |
| U3-08 | Migrate every v1–v5 project explicitly to schema v6 | Reset old Oracle state; make v5 the minimum supported version | Existing projects, approvals, run recovery, and transcripts must remain usable | Legacy projects become confirmed saved work, old Oracle summaries/questions are retained in structured intake, and repeated migration remains deterministic |
| U3-09 | Import only public, credential-free HTTPS repositories with a noninteractive Git subprocess | Accept SSH/private URLs; rely on ambient credential helpers; show clone output | Embedded/ambient credentials and raw Git errors could leak secrets, and redirects can change the trust boundary | Userinfo/query/fragment/nonstandard ports/private DNS are rejected; credential helpers, prompts, and redirects are disabled; output is discarded and failures use a fixed safe message |

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U4-01 | Validate every Architect candidate against a section-specific content contract | Trust the model; enforce a minimum word count | Word count rewards padding and does not prove that a plan covers its dependencies, risks, decisions, or acceptance criteria | Each of the eight sections declares required topics, detail guidance, dependencies, risk/decision requirements, acceptance criteria, and required headings; validation is structural and topic-based |
| U4-02 | Generate a `PENDING` candidate instead of replacing the draft | Apply the Architect reply immediately and mark downstream stale | The user must be able to inspect the complete revision before it replaces approved or draft work | `POST /api/sections/:id/revisions` queues the Architect; the current section is untouched until an explicit accept |
| U4-03 | Require an explicit accept/reject decision and bind it to the candidate base version/hash | Accept by latest content; auto-accept if the contract passes | A section can change while a candidate is being reviewed; silent overwrite is unacceptable | Accept fails with a conflict if the base changed; the user can request a fresh candidate or discard the old one |
| U4-04 | Keep acceptance separate from approval | Treat accepting a revision as approval | The user may accept wording but still want a separate approval gate; approvals are exact-version security boundaries | Accepting sets the section to `DRAFT` at the candidate version; `approveSection` remains the only path to `APPROVED` |

## Upgrade Phase 5 — focused workshop and reorganized OpenCode controls

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U5-01 | Present one primary task and move outline, memory, and activity into disclosure drawers | Keep the three-column permanent rail; add more panels beside the main task | The main task must be understandable without opening technical machinery, and empty panels should not reserve space | The main document is a single centered column; outline and memory are collapsed `<details>` drawers |
| U5-02 | Rename Run Inspector to **Activity & results** and organize it into Progress, Changes, and Checks | Keep one mixed “native runs” list | Users need to know whether a run is progressing, what changed, and what was actually checked without reading technical rows | The first three sections answer those questions; the component keeps the read-only honesty note |
| U5-03 | Hide Activity & results when no operation or evidence exists | Show an empty inspector permanently | An empty technical panel is visual noise and implies a run exists | The drawer is omitted until relevant; an active or abandoned run opens it automatically |
| U5-04 | Move native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, provider payloads, and the transcript under Technical details or Advanced diagnostics | Show IDs and raw rows in the primary view | Operational facts are useful but not the main task; raw transcripts are diagnostic material | Primary sections stay readable; the technical disclosure remains available and redacted |
| U5-05 | Replace Session notes with Project memory covering decisions, user answers, assumptions, constraints, and unresolved questions | Keep the latest transcript excerpts as the memory surface | Users need the durable project record, not a truncated chat feed | Project memory is editable; the raw transcript moves to Advanced diagnostics |
| U5-06 | Persist memory edits through `POST /api/memory`, appending a new active entry and superseding the corrected one | Mutate an existing entry in place; add a second state schema | The existing memory shape already supports status/supersedesId; audit history must survive corrections | Corrections are explicit and auditable; no schema migration is required |
| U5-07 | Split OpenCode controls into Model & connection, a contextual permission request, and Advanced diagnostics; load advanced data only on open | Keep one `<details>` containing every harness control; load sessions/usage on mount | Permissions must be impossible to miss, while sessions, agents, commands, skills, MCP, LSP, formatters, revert, export, and transcripts are diagnostic | The permission alert sits outside collapsed details; advanced sessions/usage are fetched when the panel opens |
| U5-08 | Keep the focused layout accessible on mobile and keyboard; move focus to the main task on stage change and announce busy/permission state | Rely on visual placement and native details behavior alone | The layout change must not make the workflow unreachable by keyboard or screen reader | Drawers are native disclosures, the main task receives focus after a stage change, and a polite live region reports run/permission state |

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U6-01 | Use one canonical fixture in `src/shared/demo.ts` for the guided sample, landing preview, visual tests, screenshots, and evidence examples | Keep separate landing operations/evidence and demo fixture | Two sources produced contradictory PASS and FAIL states for the same sample | `src/web/content/landing.ts` keeps copy only; every operation, evidence row, capability, and preview step derives from the canonical fixture |
| U6-02 | Replace the campus umbrella scenario with Driftwatch, an abandoned open-source issue-triage CLI | Keep the umbrella scenario and relabel it; invent a sponsor product | The product is about reviving unfinished work, and the sample must show one coherent idea, plan, bounded change, test, and review | All eight sections, diff, verification, Witness findings, landing preview, and screenshots describe the same Driftwatch change |
| U6-03 | Make the landing story hero → four-stage workflow → sample project → why OpenCode → local setup/privacy → FAQ/final CTA | Keep the previous positioning/modes/controls/recommendation stack | The page had too many competing sections and technical facts before the user outcome | One obvious primary CTA; the workflow and sample carry the product story |
| U6-04 | Keep **Try the example** primary and **Run locally** secondary; remove the duplicate “Watch the guided workflow” action | Three equal demo/watch/live actions | Visitors need one obvious next step; presentation mode remains available inside `/demo` | The hero and final CTA share the same primary/secondary hierarchy; no competing watch button |
| U6-05 | Remove the static idea-to-tool recommendation block | Make it interactive or leave it static | It was not capability-driven and added a table of invented guidance to the landing page | No recommendation fixtures or table remain; a future interactive recommender would need a new phase |
| U6-06 | Move sample provenance, fixture version, technical caveats, and the evidence inspector under `<details>` | Keep the full honesty panel permanently expanded | The main story should read in plain language, while technical proof stays inspectable | A concise “recorded sample” label stays visible; details expand on demand |
| U6-07 | Treat the hackathon theme as the workflow itself, not decorative badges | Add sponsor/prize badges or fake contest results | The product’s value is finishing an abandoned project through honest stages | Copy and sample focus on the abandoned project, bounded change, and evidence; no placement or prize claim |
| U6-08 | Replace the generic hero with a bespoke four-spirit workshop illustration and responsive variants | Keep the existing generic workshop image; use pure CSS | The hero must show the four spirits and the abandoned-project bench at a glance | New source master plus AVIF/WebP/JPEG variants; source is documented and excluded from the bundle |
| U6-09 | Reduce oversized display type, glass cards, pills, outlines, glows, and monospace labels on the landing page | Keep the previous maximal treatment | The page should feel intentional at desktop and mobile scale rather than loud everywhere | Smaller display scale, flatter sections, fewer card borders, and UI-font eyebrows replace mono labels |
| U6-10 | Add fixture-consistency and visual-regression coverage instead of relying on copy review | Snapshot the landing only; trust manual inspection | The previous contradiction was invisible to typecheck and unit tests | Unit tests assert both pages use the same fixture outcome; a Playwright test compares the landing and `/demo`; snapshots cover the new layout |
| U6-11 | Keep schema v7 and add no migration | Bump the schema for a demo-only change | The canonical fixture is not persisted user state | Saved projects remain compatible; only the internal `DEMO_FIXTURE_VERSION` changed |

## Open follow-ups (post-release)

- A real recorded demo and final submission assets remain separate acceptance work.
- The free-model route remains account-dependent and time-limited.
- A public hosted URL is not asserted until a deployment is verified.
- Any future change to the asset budget or claims requires updating `docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` and `docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md`.

input.newString:
## Platform Phase 7 — macOS support

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P7-01 | Replace `@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline` with the official `@opencode/cli` meta package at the same pinned version | Keep a Linux package plus manually select per-platform packages; download binaries at runtime | The official package selects the native binary for Linux x64, macOS arm64, and macOS x64 during install and keeps the CLI version identical to `@opencode/client` | The lockfile carries `@opencode/cli` and all platform optional dependencies at `2.0.32`; no user-facing command names a Linux package path |
| P7-02 | Resolve the executable at runtime in one platform-aware module, preferring a compatible global `opencode` | Hardcode the vendored path; always use the local package; always require a global install | Users may have npm, Homebrew, or package-manager OpenCode already; a global install may be older than the pin | Order is explicit `UB_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE`, compatible `PATH`, then the pinned local binary; an incompatible global is skipped so the local pin can still run |
| P7-03 | Gate support to Linux x64, macOS arm64, and macOS x64 and emit `OPENCODE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` elsewhere | Treat every npm-supported platform as supported | The phase has automated evidence only for those three; claiming Windows or Linux ARM64 would violate the evidence rule | Unsupported hosts fail before probing a binary; docs and CI use the same three-platform list |
| P7-04 | Keep `render-start.ts` as the Render-only supervisor but route it through the shared resolver | Maintain a separate Render binary path; remove the supervisor | Render needs a process parent and persistent XDG paths; local development must not depend on Render behavior | Render-specific values are environment variables; the resolver is identical locally and hosted |
| P7-05 | Derive the Playwright data directory from `os.tmpdir()` and add macOS browser paths | Keep `/tmp` and Linux-only Chrome paths | Local visual tests must run on macOS without a patched config | The web server uses the host temporary directory; system Chrome/Chromium candidates include the standard macOS application locations |
| P7-06 | Resolve the host temporary directory and add macOS broad roots in workspace security | Rely on string equality with `/tmp` | macOS aliases `/tmp` and the host temporary directory through `/private`; a resolved path must not bypass the broad-root check | Broad roots include `/Users`, `/Volumes`, `/System`, `/private`, `/private/tmp`, `/private/var/tmp`, and `/private/var/folders`; the real temporary root is rejected |
| P7-07 | Verify Linux and both macOS architectures in CI, including an OpenCode server smoke test | Claim macOS from documentation; run only unit tests | Acceptance requires automated or recorded manual evidence per claimed host | Matrix jobs run install, CLI resolution, typecheck, tests, build, workspace safety, and a no-inference server start/version smoke |
| P7-08 | Keep the setup UI and docs platform-neutral: `npx --no-install opencode` plus npm and Homebrew install options | Show the vendored Linux path; omit install alternatives | The setup tabs are user-facing and previously named a Linux-only package | No setup command contains `cli-linux`; docs distinguish Linux from macOS evidence and mark Windows/Linux ARM64 unsupported |

## Open follow-ups (post-release)

input.newString:
Phase 6 acceptance passed on 2026-11-01. No live provider inference was used.

## Platform Phase 7 — macOS support

### Outcome

The local workshop now supports Linux x64, macOS Apple Silicon, and macOS Intel. The Linux-only OpenCode package is gone. One resolver prefers a compatible global `opencode` on `PATH`, then the official cross-platform `@opencode/cli` binary pinned by the lockfile. Unsupported hosts, missing or non-executable binaries, incompatible versions, and server start failures produce distinct, path-safe diagnostics. Render keeps its process-supervisor behavior through environment configuration rather than a hardcoded Linux executable.

**Phase commit:** `feat(platform): add macOS OpenCode support`.

### Work units

| Unit | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P7-1 dependency | Replaced `@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline` with official `@opencode/cli@2.0.32`; the lockfile pins CLI and `@opencode/client` together and carries all platform optional dependencies | `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tests/platform.test.ts` |
| P7-2 resolver | Explicit `UB_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE` → compatible `PATH` → lockfile binary; incompatible global installs are skipped; no executable path is logged | `src/server/opencode/executable.ts`, `tests/platform.test.ts` |
| P7-3 platform gate | Only `linux-x64`, `darwin-arm64`, and `darwin-x64` are claimed; other hosts fail before probing with `OPENCODE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` | `SUPPORTED_OPENCODE_PLATFORMS`, platform tests |
| P7-4 Render isolation | `render-start.ts` uses the shared resolver; XDG and port values come from environment or `UB_DATA_DIR`, not hardcoded Linux paths | `src/server/render-start.ts`, `.env.example` |
| P7-5 workspace safety | Broad-root rejection covers `/Users`, `/Volumes`, `/System`, `/private`, `/private/tmp`, `/private/var/tmp`, and `/private/var/folders`; the resolved host temporary root is rejected | `src/server/security/workspace.ts`, `tests/security.test.ts` |
| P7-6 temp and browser paths | Playwright data uses `os.tmpdir()`; system browser candidates include standard macOS application paths | `playwright.config.ts` |
| P7-7 diagnostics | CLI missing, unsupported architecture, incompatible/untested version, permission denial, and server start failure have distinct codes and repairs; the doctor and smoke scripts are path-safe | `src/server/opencode/executable.ts`, `scripts/opencode-platform-diagnostic.ts`, `scripts/opencode-smoke.ts` |
| P7-8 setup UI and docs | Setup tabs use `npx --no-install opencode`; npm and Homebrew install commands are documented; Linux and macOS evidence is separated | `src/web/setup.ts`, README, `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md`, `docs/OPENCODE_INTEGRATION.md` |
| P7-9 CI matrix | Linux x64, macOS arm64, and macOS x64 run install, CLI resolution, typecheck, tests, build, workspace safety, and a no-inference OpenCode server smoke | `.github/workflows/sentry-release.yml` |

### Acceptance status

- [x] Linux behavior remains operational; the full local matrix and OpenCode smoke pass.
- [x] No user-facing setup command contains `cli-linux` or a Linux-only package path.
- [x] macOS arm64 and x64 resolutions use the same resolver; injected host tests cover both, and the CI jobs exercise the real binaries.
- [x] Workspace security rejects macOS broad roots and the resolved temporary root.
- [x] Setup documentation distinguishes locally verified Linux from CI-gated macOS and marks Windows/Linux ARM64 unsupported.
- [x] Typecheck, **200 tests**, build, budget, visual suite, platform diagnostics, and OpenCode smoke pass locally.
- [x] Diff review found no secrets, debugging output, or unrelated changes.

Platform Phase 7 acceptance passed on 2026-11-01. macOS execution is delegated to the `macos-15` and `macos-15-intel` CI jobs; local execution on this Linux host cannot stand in for that evidence and is not claimed as manual macOS proof. No live provider inference was used.

# Evidence index and requirements matrix

**Status:** Upgrade Phase 6 complete and verified.
**Owner:** Engineering.

## Requirements-to-evidence matrix

| Area | Requirement | Status | Evidence | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Project source | Every fresh project chooses new, local, remote, or saved work before Oracle | VERIFIED | `tests/oracle-discovery.test.ts`; source-first workshop rendering; `PROJECT_SOURCE_REQUIRED` server gate | Demo fixture carries an explicit `DEMO` source |
| Project source | Local repositories pass existing workspace-security rules and private paths stay server-only | VERIFIED | `tests/oracle-discovery.test.ts`, `tests/security.test.ts`; public project serialization assertion | Selection validates but does not assess repository contents |
| Project source | Remote URL is credential-free/public HTTPS, staged without import, then imported into a managed workspace only after confirmation | VERIFIED | `tests/oracle-discovery.test.ts`; injected importer asserts no call before confirm and managed target after confirm | Public unauthenticated Git only; no SSH/private/submodule credentials |
| Oracle discovery | Incomplete intake produces at most three high-value questions with rationale and optional choices | VERIFIED | `tests/oracle-discovery.test.ts`; `oracleReplySchema` max-three assertion | Relevance of live model wording remains provider-dependent |
| Oracle discovery | Full discovery instructions remain active and proposal mode is server-gated on sufficient information or explicit assumptions | VERIFIED | prompt-capture and assumption-gate cases in `tests/oracle-discovery.test.ts` | No live provider inference in this phase |
| Oracle memory | Answers survive reload, corrections supersede history, and proposals distinguish facts, user decisions, and assumptions | VERIFIED | persistence/correction/proposal cases in `tests/oracle-discovery.test.ts`; schema v7 round-trip/migration tests | Transcript retention remains bounded separately |
| Architect revisions | Every section has a content contract with required topics, detail guidance, dependencies, risks, decisions, and acceptance criteria; padded word count alone fails | VERIFIED | `src/shared/section-contracts.ts`; `tests/revisions.test.ts` (all eight compliant drafts, padded-word rejection) | Contracts judge structure and coverage, not prose quality |
| Architect revisions | A change request generates a candidate and never overwrites the current draft; accept/reject/supersede are explicit | VERIFIED | `tests/revisions.test.ts`, `tests/experience.test.ts` route case, `tests/http-workflow.test.ts` accept case | No live provider inference |
| Architect revisions | Acceptance is separate from approval and marks only transitive downstream approvals stale | VERIFIED | `tests/revisions.test.ts` stale-approval matrix; `tests/http-workflow.test.ts` approval-after-accept case | Unrelated approvals stay valid by design |
| Architect revisions | Complete revision and unified/side-by-side diff are reviewable before acceptance | VERIFIED | `src/web/components/RevisionReview.tsx`, `RevisionDiff.tsx`; `tests/revisions.test.ts` diff assertions | Visual snapshot suite does not yet capture a live candidate state |

| Run recovery | Idle session without a confirmed outcome is never success | VERIFIED | `tests/observable-runs.test.ts` unknown-outcome test; `inspect` maps idle-without-outcome to `unknown` | — |
| Run recovery | Confirm-failure retry creates a lineage-tracked operation and cannot duplicate the native run | VERIFIED | `tests/observable-runs.test.ts` retry test (`retryOf`, unresolved/active/final-state gates) | Manual resume of a lost native session is limited to reconciliation |

| Run controls | Elapsed time and Continue waiting / Reconcile now / Open in OpenCode / Cancel / Retry / Mark abandoned controls visible in Activity & results | VERIFIED | `src/web/components/RunInspector.tsx` recovery panel; `tests/web.test.ts` renders; workshop visual suite | Activity & results is absent until an operation or check exists |
| Focused workshop | One primary task, compact model/connection header, collapsible project outline, contextual activity drawer, no permanent technical rail | VERIFIED | `src/web/workshop/WorkshopPage.tsx`, `src/web/styles.css`; `tests/visual/landing.spec.ts` wide/narrow captures | Automated visual checks do not replace a full screen-reader audit |
| Activity & results | Progress, Changes, and Checks are separate; native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, and provider payloads are under Technical details | VERIFIED | `RunInspector.tsx`; `tests/web.test.ts` server-render sections; `run-inspector.png` | The technical section is read-only |

# Tool and capability catalog

**Status:** Current release inventory.
**Owner:** Engineering.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01.

This catalog distinguishes what the product **uses** and what is only a **documented future possibility**. A listed tool is not an install, account, endorsement, or partner-category proof.

## Core tools

| Tool | Role | Status | Evidence/limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenCode 2.0.32 | Agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, sessions, interruption | **Integrated foundation** | Exact client/server pin; production code uses the official client through the safe network layer. Live compatibility probe passed without inference. |
| OpenCode model catalog | Any model the connected account reports as available | **Integrated; model-dependent** | New projects default to all accessible models. Free/local-only policy and optional spending limits are available. Paid/unknown-price routes require explicit confirmation; no silent substitution. |
| Node.js 22.14+ | Runtime, build, and bounded Node check | **Required** | Tested on 22.22.1; `engines` minimum 22.14. |
| React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 8 | Browser interface and build | **Integrated** | Production build and bundle budget pass. |
| Hono 4 + `@hono/node-server` | HTTP API and static serving | **Integrated** | Security middleware, validation, SSE, and static containment are tested. |
| Zod 4 | Shared request/state/output validation | **Integrated** | Workflow schema v7, explicit v1–v6 migration, project-source/Oracle intake, reviewable candidate revisions, section contracts, model policy, provider-error, and engine/discovery contracts. |
| Motion 14 + Lucide | Purposeful motion and icons | **Integrated** | Free libraries only; reduced-motion fallback tested. No second animation framework. |

## Verification and operations tools

| Tool | Role | Status | Evidence/limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node test runner | Unit/integration/component tests | **Integrated** | 186 passing tests. |
| Playwright 1.62 | Visual, keyboard, contrast, zoom, reduced-motion, overflow, and canonical-sample tests | **Integrated** | 20 passing tests with committed snapshots; uses system Chromium. |
| `scripts/check-budget.mjs` | Production bundle/asset budget | **Integrated** | Passes: initial JS 201.3 KiB gzip, all JS 279.9 KiB (290 KiB budget), CSS 17.0 KiB (18 KiB budget), hero 581.2 KiB. |
| `scripts/preflight.mjs` | Read-only environment diagnostic | **Integrated** | Checks toolchain, DNS, loopback, OpenCode CLI/help, Git reads, Entire status. Not an integration proof. |
| `scripts/opencode-live-diagnostic.ts` | Opt-in compatibility probe | **Integrated; run in Phase 9** | Server 2.0.32, catalog, disposable session create/read/remove. No prompt/model call. |
| Render | Optional demo or private hosting | **Documented; not deployed** | `render.demo.yaml` and `render.yaml` reviewed statically. No live URL asserted. |
| GitHub Actions | Typecheck/test/build quality gate | **Configured** | `.github/workflows/sentry-release.yml` runs the quality gate; Render owns production source-map upload. |

## Observability and development evidence

| Tool | Role | Status | Evidence/limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sentry Node/browser SDKs | Optional errors, traces, replay, profiling, metadata-only agent spans | **Configured; live release proof not run** | SDK collection is disabled for prompts/bodies/headers/identity; redaction is tested. A live event/release/source-map/trace check needs authorized credentials and a deployment. |
| Entire | Development-session capture and checkpoints | **Development record only** | Repository has Entire hooks/checkpoints from earlier phases. It is not a runtime product feature and no public transcript is shared. |
| Backboard R-CLI | Candidate build-process contribution | **Not integrated** | No API key/tooling in this environment; no session, diff, check, or category claim. |

## Recommendation policy

There is no landing-page idea-to-tool recommender in this release. The previous static table was removed in Upgrade Phase 6 because it was not interactive or capability-driven. A future recommender must be tied to the discovered OpenCode capability set, cite source freshness, show permissions and observed outcomes, and never turn a recommendation into an approval or a Maker scope grant.

Source freshness for this catalog:

| Claim | Source | Last checked |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode 2.0.32 client/server compatibility | Local pinned binary + Phase 9 live compatibility probe | 2026-10-31 |
| Model access, pricing, and spending policy | OpenCode model catalog; `.env.example`; model-access and connection tests | 2026-11-01 |
| Sentry privacy configuration | SDK code, redaction tests, deployment docs | 2026-10-31 |
| Entire capture presence | Repository hooks/checkpoints and prior phase records | 2026-10-31 |
| Render templates | `render.yaml`, `render.demo.yaml` static review | 2026-10-31 |
| Playwright/browser availability | Visual suite against system Chromium | 2026-11-01 |

if (!serverVersion) blocked(...)

152:- The workshop uses non-interactive stage items: they do not pretend to be clickable tabs. `aria-current="step"` marks the current stage.
153:- The guided sample passes `onSelect`, so each stage is a real button labeled “Inspect Oracle/Architect/Maker/Witness”. Selecting a tab pauses playback and shows that spirit's sample workspace. `aria-current="step"` still marks the inspected stage.
160:- The layout is: intro/honesty panel → playback controls → four-spirit tabs → guided beat + spirit workspace → Activity & results → representative diff/check → Witness findings → character gallery/recovery → clean exit.
163:- Tabs are available during playback. Inspecting a tab pauses auto-advance and shows “Playback paused so you can inspect …”. Resume with Play.
178:- The project outline is a native `<details>` drawer with the approval progress and selectable section cards. It opens without hiding the main task.
231:- Tabbed commands with roving tabindex, Arrow/Home/End keyboard support, `aria-selected`, and `aria-controls`.
234:- Active tab is indicated by border, background, and color, not color alone.
296:- Minimum 44px targets for actions, tabs, stage rows, and sample controls.
297:- Tabs use roving tabindex and full arrow-key support.
298:- Stage strip is a list; the sample's inspectable stages are real buttons with visible focus rings.
356:The initial route is the landing page. Workshop and sample are lazy-loaded (69.4 KiB and 5.6 KiB gzip, plus 3.5 KiB shared stage tabs). The canonical fixture is shared by the eager landing chunk and the lazy sample chunk; the sample chunk adds the playback reducer and guided UI. This removes the previous duplicate landing state and raises initial JS to 201.3 KiB while lowering all-JS to 279.9 KiB. The workshop chunk includes the connection/discovery wizard, project memory, Activity & results, and lazy Advanced diagnostics. The hero transfers **15.6–56.3 KiB** as AVIF on a typical wide viewport and **32.8–52.4 KiB** as AVIF on mobile depending on pixel density; the total covers all breakpoints and formats, not one visit.
361:- Update this table deliberately if a budget changes; do not silently raise it.
381:- Hosted-sample copy says there is no OpenCode, provider, session token, visitor persistence, or repository. `/workshop` is a read-only notice with exits to `/demo` and local setup.
384:- There is no landing-page recommender in this release. The static recommendation table was removed in Upgrade Phase 6; a future recommender must be capability-driven, cite source freshness, and never imply an install, paid model, arbitrary shell, or approval.
386:- The final accessibility matrix covers keyboard focus, dialog Escape, setup-tab arrow keys, 200% text zoom, 390px/wide layouts, overflow, reduced motion, contrast, and relevant screen-reader/live-region semantics.

content.text:
Two issues:
1. macOS broad root test: on macOS `tmpdir()` returns `/var/folders/...` and `realpathSync(tmpdir())` returns `/private/var/folders/...`. Our test loops `["/", homedir(), tmpdir(), process.cwd()]`. One of these isn't rejected. Likely `homedir()`? On GitHub mac runner home is `/Users/runner`. broadRoots includes /Users but home check uses canonical(homedir()) = `/Users/runner`; resolved homedir same. Should reject. `tmpdir()` canonical? We compare resolved path to canonical temp. `resolved = normalized(tmpdir())` = `/var/folders/.../T`; canonical temp = `/private/var/folders/.../T`, so not equal. But broadRoots includes `/private/var/folders` only exact, not nested. So `tmpdir()` (unresolved) isn't rejected. We should compare both resolved and canonical forms. In `assertNotBroadRoot`, compute `const canonicalResolved = canonical(path)` maybe and check against temp/home/repository/broad roots. But if path is a symlink to a broad root, we should reject. In assertNotBroadRoot sync, `canonical(path)` for a child under temp? It would give `/private/var/folders/.../project`, not equal temp. Fine. Add:
```
const realResolved = canonical(path);
const isBroad = (candidate) => candidate === filesystemRoot || broadRoots.has(candidate) || candidate === home || candidate === temporary || candidate === repository || candidate === dirname(home)
if (isBroad(resolved) || isBroad(realResolved)) throw
```
But `filesystemRoot = parse(resolved).root`; canonical same. Good.
This fixes macOS tmpdir unresolved and any symlink to broad root. Also could use canonical path for repository.
Modify.

2. Linux reconnect test flake? "reconnecting after a server restart reconciles..." expected 'ses_maker_restart' actual null. It passed locally every time. CI failure likely timing/race. glob 14 is ESM. Sentry bundler plugin likely imports glob; if its package is ESM or bundles, could work. But overriding transitive to a new ESM major is risky, exactly "carefully, without combining unrelated major migrations". Maybe better leave moderate advisories documented as known limitation? But requirement 5 says "Upgrade vulnerable dependencies carefully, including Sentry packages"—we are already at latest Sentry. Could attempt override and run build/tests. If works, eliminates audit advisories. But it's a major override. Is that acceptable? It is a security hardening phase. We can add:
```
"overrides": {
  "glob": "14.0.3",
  "minimatch": "11.0.3"
}
```

  1. Source select

  5. Approve all sections
  6. Grant maker scope

Two issues:
1. modelClipped false because inline is inline element, clientWidth/scrollWidth not meaningful. Use display block? `header-model-inline` is span but in flex header, display default inline; computed width constrained by content? We can check `getBoundingClientRect().width <= 22ch` and `scrollWidth` maybe 0. Better wrap in a block with width 320? Or measure `model.getBoundingClientRect().width` <= 300 and `getComputedStyle.textOverflow === "ellipsis"`. To prove clipping, compare `scrollWidth` of a block. Set `inline.style.display = "block"` in test? That changes CSS behavior but still text-overflow. Better set host width 320 and inline as block? In actual header, flex item has max-width and overflow hidden; inline's width is constrained. `scrollWidth` on inline might equal clientWidth 0. Could use `model.getBoundingClientRect().width <= 22 * 8` (approx) and `model.scrollWidth` maybe not. Simpler assert `model.getBoundingClientRect().width < host.getBoundingClientRect().width` and textOverflow ellipsis, overflow hidden. That proves it doesn't expand. For strong evidence, set `inline.style.display = "block"` then check scrollWidth > clientWidth; but CSS class still. We can in injection set `inline.style.display = "block"` and `inline.style.width = "220px"`? Then artificial. Better create a `.header-model-inline` block inside host (a span with display block) and check. But actual header span is flex item and behaves like block due flex item. Setting display block mimics. Use `inline.style.display = "block"` plus host width 320. Then `scrollWidth > clientWidth` should be true. Add that in test and assert. This is a test of the class under flex-like width. Acceptable.

Requirement offline state. We should improve `WorkshopPage` catch to map network failures to friendly message. Currently line 167 chooses message based on `caught instanceof ApiError`? Could improve responsive CSS at <= 900 or 768: hide `.header-model-inline` maybe, allow brand no wrap, hide "Overview"/"Demo"? Need inspect header CSS.
